examples.question_text:
A polynomial $P(x)$ is divided by $(x-3)(x+2)$, with quotient $Q(x)$ and remainder $R(x)$.
(a) Explain why $R(x)$ can be written as $ax+b$.
(b) Write the division identity.
examples.solution_text:
(a) The divisor has degree $2$, so a nonzero remainder has degree $1$ or $0$. The form $R(x)=ax+b$ also includes a constant when $a=0$ and zero when $a=b=0$.

(b) $P(x)=(x-3)(x+2)Q(x)+ax+b$

examples.question_text:
(a) When $P(x)$ is divided by $x^2-36$, the remainder is $2x-5$. Find the remainder when $P(x)$ is divided by $x+6$.
(b) When $F(x)$ is divided by $(3x-2)(x+4)$, the remainder is $6x+1$. Find the remainder when $F(x)$ is divided by $3x-2$.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Factorise the quadratic divisor:
$x^2-36=(x-6)(x+6)$.

$\begin{aligned}P(x)&=(x-6)(x+6)Q(x)+2x-5\\P(-6)&=(-6-6)(0)Q(-6)+2(-6)-5\\&=-17\end{aligned}$

The remainder is $-17$.

(b) The divisor $3x-2$ is zero at $x=\frac{2}{3}$.

$\begin{aligned}F(x)&=(3x-2)(x+4)Q(x)+6x+1\\F\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)&=0+6\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)+1\\&=5\end{aligned}$

The remainder is $5$.

examples.question_text:
A polynomial $P(x)$ is divided by $(x-3)(x+2)$.
Given $P(3)=11$ and $P(-2)=-4$, find its remainder.
examples.solution_text:
Write the remainder as $ax+b$:
$P(x)=(x-3)(x+2)Q(x)+ax+b$.

Substitute the roots of the divisor:
$\begin{aligned}3a+b&=11\\-2a+b&=-4\end{aligned}$

Subtract the second equation from the first:
$\begin{aligned}5a&=15\\a&=3\end{aligned}$

Substitute into $3a+b=11$:
$\begin{aligned}b&=11-3(3)\\&=2\end{aligned}$

The remainder is $3x+2$.

examples.question_text: Find the remainder when $P(x)=x^3+2x^2-9x+7$ is divided by $x^2-9$.
examples.solution_text:
Since $x^2-9=(x-3)(x+3)$, write
$P(x)=(x-3)(x+3)Q(x)+ax+b$.

Evaluate at both roots:
$\begin{aligned}P(3)&=3^3+2(3)^2-9(3)+7\\&=25\\P(-3)&=(-3)^3+2(-3)^2-9(-3)+7\\&=25\end{aligned}$

Hence
$\begin{aligned}3a+b&=25\\-3a+b&=25\end{aligned}$

Subtract the equations:
$\begin{aligned}6a&=0\\a&=0\\b&=25\end{aligned}$

The remainder is the constant $25$.

examples.question_text:
A polynomial leaves remainder $2$ when divided by $x+3$ and remainder $17$ when divided by $x-2$.
Find the remainder when it is divided by $(x+3)(x-2)$.
examples.solution_text:
By the remainder theorem, $P(-3)=2$ and $P(2)=17$.

Write
$P(x)=(x+3)(x-2)Q(x)+ax+b$.

Substitute the roots:
$\begin{aligned}-3a+b&=2\\2a+b&=17\end{aligned}$

Subtract the first equation from the second:
$\begin{aligned}5a&=15\\a&=3\end{aligned}$

Substitute into $2a+b=17$:
$\begin{aligned}b&=17-2(3)\\&=11\end{aligned}$

The remainder is $3x+11$.

examples.question_text:
When $P(x)=x^5+2x^3+ax+b$ is divided by $x^2-1$, the remainder is $7x+4$.
Find $a$ and $b$.
examples.solution_text:
Since $x^2-1=(x-1)(x+1)$, the division identity is
$P(x)=(x-1)(x+1)Q(x)+7x+4$.

Substitute $x=1$:
$\begin{aligned}1+2+a+b&=7+4\\a+b&=8\end{aligned}$

Substitute $x=-1$:
$\begin{aligned}-1-2-a+b&=-7+4\\-a+b&=0\end{aligned}$

Subtract the second equation from the first:
$\begin{aligned}2a&=8\\a&=4\end{aligned}$

Then $b=a=4$.

Therefore $a=4$ and $b=4$.

examples.question_text:
When $P(x)$ is divided by $x^2-7$, the remainder is $3x-2$.
Find the remainder when $P(x)+P(-x)$ is divided by $x^2-7$.
examples.solution_text:
Write the division identity:
$P(x)=(x^2-7)Q(x)+3x-2$.

Replace $x$ by $-x$:
$\begin{aligned}P(-x)&=\bigl((-x)^2-7\bigr)Q(-x)+3(-x)-2\\&=(x^2-7)Q(-x)-3x-2\end{aligned}$

Add the identities and collect terms:
$\begin{aligned}P(x)+P(-x)&=(x^2-7)Q(x)+3x-2\\&\quad +(x^2-7)Q(-x)-3x-2\\&=(x^2-7)\bigl(Q(x)+Q(-x)\bigr)-4\end{aligned}$

The remainder is $-4$.

All 24 assessment locators are mapped; accepted assessments were neither altered nor re-audited. Questions and solutions are separate editable fields, with single-dollar mathematics and renderer-inherited blue solutions. examples.derivation: The divisor has degree 2, so the remainder is ax+b, covering linear, constant and zero remainders. The identity is P(x)=(x-3)(x+2)Q(x)+ax+b.
For (a), x²-36=(x-6)(x+6), and substitution at -6 gives 2(-6)-5=-17. For (b), 3x-2 vanishes at 2/3, giving 6(2/3)+1=5.
The root substitutions give 3a+b=11 and -2a+b=-4. Subtraction gives 5a=15, so a=3 and b=2. The remainder is 3x+2.
P(3)=27+18-27+7=25 and P(-3)=-27+18+27+7=25. Thus 3a+b=25 and -3a+b=25, giving a=0 and b=25. The remainder is 25.
The given linear remainders give P(-3)=2 and P(2)=17. Hence -3a+b=2 and 2a+b=17. Subtraction gives a=3, then b=11. The remainder is 3x+11.
At x=1, 3+a+b=11, so a+b=8. At x=-1, -3-a+b=-3, so -a+b=0. Therefore a=4 and b=4. This follows the supplied Book 3 Mastery Q18 method and preserves the accepted assessment's degree-5 scope.
Substitution of -x leaves x²-7 unchanged and changes 3x-2 to -3x-2. Adding the identities gives P(x)+P(-x)=(x²-7)(Q(x)+Q(-x))-4. The remainder is -4.
